title: Design System: Autonomous Code Review Engine — Dashboard

title.purpose: The one h1 per panel ("Dashboard"). Not bold — position and color carry hierarchy, not weight.

body.purpose: Default text: stat values, table cells, form inputs.

label.purpose: Stat labels, field hints, field labels, timestamps — small and muted.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Popups and dialogs only — the system's one shadow, signaling transience.

shadows.name: tooltip
shadows.purpose: The small info-icon tooltip — a lighter variant of the overlay shadow.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Chevron rotation, tooltip fade-in — the system's only transition timing.

components.name: Control Button
components.description: The default pill button — topbar icon buttons, panel-nav tabs, table row actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-control { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.4rem 0.9rem; font-size: 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-control:hover { border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-btn-control:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-control:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Nav Tab (active)
components.description: The active variant of the panel-nav pill tab — the only nav state carrying accent color.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { gap: 0.4rem; } .ds-nav-item-active { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); } .ds-nav-item svg { width: 1.05rem; height: 1.05rem; display: block; flex: none; }

components.name: Submit Button
components.description: The one filled-accent button in the system — used only for the login form's single action.
components.css: .ds-btn-submit { width: 100%; padding: 0.6rem; border: none; border-radius: 0.4rem; background: var(--accent); color: #fff; font-size: 0.95rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-submit:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Default text/password field — visually identical to a Control Button at rest.
components.css: .ds-input { font: inherit; width: 100%; padding: 0.5rem 0.6rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0.4rem; background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); font-size: 0.95rem; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-input[readonly] { opacity: 0.7; }

components.name: Stat Tile
components.description: The primary at-a-glance metric card — flat, bordered, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-stat-tile { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0.6rem; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; } .ds-stat-label { color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 0.8rem; } .ds-stat-value { font-size: 1.4rem; font-weight: 600; margin-top: 0.15rem; }

components.name: Tile Chip
components.description: Small nested-content chip inside a stat tile — the one component that uses fill instead of an outline.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: var(--surface-2); border-radius: 0.3rem; padding: 0.15rem 0.45rem; font-size: 0.8rem; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Review Card
components.description: A collapsible row summarizing one PR review, expandable to show findings.
components.html: ✓ postedPR #142⌄
components.css: .ds-review-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0.6rem; overflow: hidden; } .ds-review-row { position: relative; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 0.7rem 1rem; padding-inline-end: 2.25rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-status-ok { color: var(--ok); } .ds-chevron { position: absolute; top: 0.75rem; inset-inline-end: 1rem; transition: transform 0.15s ease; } .ds-review-row[aria-expanded="true"] .ds-chevron { transform: rotate(180deg); }

components.name: Popup / Dialog
components.description: Positioned menu (theme/language pickers) and modal confirmation — the system's only shadowed surfaces, signaling transience.
components.html: Theme
components.css: .ds-popup { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0.75rem; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; min-width: 220px; max-width: min(90vw, 320px); box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2); } .ds-popup h2 { margin: 0 0 0.75rem; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-radio-group { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-radio-group label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.35rem 0.25rem; cursor: pointer; font-size: 0.95rem; }

narrative.overview:
This is a gauge cluster, not a storefront. One person built and runs this bot; this surface exists so that person can glance at it, know whether it's healthy, and make one small adjustment, then look away. Every visual decision optimizes for that: flat surfaces that don't compete for attention, one signal color reserved for "this is active or actionable," and enough restraint that a table full of environment variables or a findings feed doesn't turn into visual noise.

The system is calm, precise, and unadorned. It explicitly rejects the SaaS-analytics-dashboard look — no gradients, no card shadows, no decorative iconography, no marketing-site polish. Depth, when it appears at all, marks something transient (a popup, a dialog) rather than dressing up permanent chrome. The palette is almost entirely neutral gray-on-white (or the dark-mode inverse); color is spent only where it means something: status, severity, or "you can act here."
keyCharacteristics: Flat-at-rest, borders instead of shadows on every persistent surface
One accent color, spent sparingly and only on actionable/active elements
Full light / dark / system theming via CSS custom properties, no light-only or dark-only assumptions baked into any component
RTL-ready throughout (logical properties: inset-inline-end, padding-inline-end, not left/right)
Severity and status communicated through color + text, never color alone

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Steady Signal Blue appears only where it means "active" or "actionable" — the current nav tab, a link, a focus ring, the one primary submit action. It never decorates a heading, an icon at rest, or a background. If a screen needs a second accent to feel finished, that's a sign the layout needs restructuring, not a second color.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Never-Color-Alone Rule
rules.body: ok/fail/severity colors always pair with text (a status word, a severity label) — never a bare colored dot or bar as the only signal, since color alone fails both colorblind users and theme edge cases.

rules.name: The Weight-Is-Rare Rule
rules.body: Font-weight above 400 is reserved for exactly two things: a stat tile's value, and a provider name in the config grid. Everywhere else, hierarchy comes from size, color, and position — not bold text.

rules.name: The Shadow-Means-Temporary Rule
rules.body: If it has a shadow, it's going to close. If it's meant to stay on screen, it gets a border instead.

dos: Do spend Steady Signal Blue only on the active/actionable element — never on a background, a heading, or a resting icon (The One Signal Rule).
Do use a border, never a shadow, to separate any surface meant to stay on screen (The Shadow-Means-Temporary Rule).
Do pair every status/severity color with a text label.

Do keep every new component themeable through the existing CSS custom properties (--bg, --surface, --text, etc.) so light/dark/system theming stays automatic — never hardcode a hex value in a new rule.
Do use logical properties (inset-inline-end, padding-inline-start) for anything positional, so RTL (Hebrew) keeps working without special-casing.
donts: Don't add a card shadow, gradient, or decorative icon anywhere — this system's whole identity is what it leaves out.
Don't introduce a second accent color. If two things need to look distinct and important at once, that's a layout problem, not a palette gap.
Don't give inputs a special focus treatment different from buttons — one focus ring style, applied uniformly, is a deliberate invariant.
Don't build a persistent sidebar. Two views live in a pill-tab row under the title; adding more views means extending that row, not introducing a new navigation paradigm.
